partnershipPlan: Two former patients and one relative from the follow-up clinic advisory group read the review's practice points before the teaching day; the nurse educator and one bedside nurse review the harms section.
socialListening: No social media listening; anonymised comments from the unit's family feedback cards since March 2025 are read for mentions of the diary.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I had lost nine days; reading my wife's pages was the first time the nightmares had a shape I could put words to.
items.implication: Keep reading with a clinician as the core of the guideline, not only writing.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Writing was the only thing I could do for him while the machines did everything else.
items.implication: Describe the diary's value to relatives as well as to patients.

items.theme: Pages I did not want him to read
items.quote: Composite paraphrase: On the worst night I wrote things I tore out before I gave it to him.
items.implication: Tell relatives they can remove or hold back entries.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: We hand the diary over at discharge and never find out what happened when they opened it.
items.implication: Recommend a planned reading at the follow-up clinic with a screen beforehand.

summary: Four composite voices on meaning, relatives' role, privacy and reading support.
